items.title: Can't stop f*cking laughing at this scroll.
items.summary:
Can't stop f*cking laughing at this scroll.

One pinned canvas, 12 scroll steps, and a full studio portfolio unrolls on a single viewport. 3D cards tilting in depth, glitch letters smearing across the screen, white flushes ripping between sections. Not a single page reload.

Break the scroll open:

1. Pinned canvas. Viewport locks, scroll drives every move.
2. 3D tile carousel. Cards tilt in perspective, swap by scroll.
3. Glitch type layer. Letters smear across the frame.
4. Hard transitions. White flush, then cloud wipe. No fade.
5. Four sections. Fortnite, Unreal Engine, WEAR GO LAND.

The studio behind the scroll is Alche, a Tokyo shop building Fortnite islands in UEFN and Unreal Engine worlds.

GPT-6 Astra builds animated one-shot scroll sites from a public prompt set. The set pins the canvas and warns against scroll hijacking.

Not coding pages. Scrolling them into the viewport.

items.title: Recent Advances in AI Are Creating a ‘Paradigm Shift’ for Robotics | Research UC Berkeley
items.summary:
In recent months, artificial intelligence agents that can reason, plan and use external tools to accomplish multistep tasks have already reshaped computer coding, online shopping, dinner reservations and cyberattacks.

Robotics might be next.

Ken Goldberg, a UC Berkeley roboticist and professor of engineering, said new models make it possible for teams of AI agents to develop robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments and revise the code when something doesn’t work. [...] Then, AI agents generate and connect these skills into a robot program. Using NVIDIA’s Isaac simulation libraries, the agents autonomously rehearse the program across task variations, identify where failures happen and refine the approach before deployment. [...] OpenAI’s recent release of its Astra model made the process even more promising, Goldberg said. His postdoctoral students Eric Kaiyuan Chen and Shuangyu Xie gave Astra access to their simulation interface and a short video of a real robot whose assignment was using a sponge to wipe ink off a metal bar. In less than an hour, the AI tool created and fine-tuned a physics simulation that accurately reproduced the video, including very realistic deformations of the sponge.

items.title: Live online certificate brings AI expertise to finance professionals | Cornell Chronicle
items.summary: That philosophy is reflected in the curriculum, which progresses from AI foundations and tools to financial use cases, responsible AI, industry applications and leadership. Participants examine applications including investment research, credit risk, fraud detection, compliance, client engagement and operational efficiency, while also considering issues such as hallucinations, data security, regulation and governance. items.title: Google AI policy forces decision for San Diego schools – NBC 7 San Diego
items.summary:
As districts consider their options, students are already seeing artificial intelligence become a more common part of everyday learning.

“I feel like I see a lot of people using AI now,” said Delilah Ortiz, a student at El Camino High School.

Some students believe the focus should be on establishing guidelines for AI use rather than banning the technology entirely. [...] San Diego County school districts face a January deadline to decide whether to opt in to Google's artificial intelligence features or lose access to the company's search engine, forcing educators to weigh the benefits of AI against concerns about student access to the technology. [...] Google plans to disable a range of AI-powered features, including Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Search in January to give school districts more control over the technology students can access. However, districts that want to continue using Google Search will have to opt in to the AI features.

items.summary:
Giai đoạn 2026-2030, Việt Nam đặt mục tiêu xy dựng ít nhất 5 phòng thí nghiệm trọng điểm và 5 phòng thí nghiệm chuyên ngành hiện đại, tập trung vào công nghệ gen, công nghệ tế bào thực vật và động vật, vi sinh vật, thú y và chẩn đoán dịch bệnh. Mục tiêu đến năm 2035, tầm nhìn đến năm 2045 là làm chủ hoàn toàn công nghệ sinh học thế hệ mới và công nghệ chỉnh sửa gen để tạo ra các sản phẩm thương mại phục vụ thị trường trong nước và xuất khẩu. [...] Được xếp vào danh mục công nghệ chiến lược cấp quốc gia, công nghệ chỉnh sửa gen, đặc biệt là CRISPR/Cas, đang mở ra vận hội lớn để nông nghiệp Việt Nam chủ động thích ứng với biến đổi khí hậu và bảo đảm an ninh lương thực.

Các chuyên gia quốc tế khẳng định, kỹ thuật chỉnh sửa gen, tiêu biểu là CRISPR/Cas, mang lại bước tiến mang tính cách mạng nhờ khả năng can thiệp chính xác, có chủ đích vào hệ gen mục tiêu mà không đưa vật liệu di truyền ngoại lai vào cơ thể sinh vật. [...] Trong định hướng phát triển khoa học, công nghệ và đổi mới sáng tạo phục vụ tái cơ cấu ngành nông nghiệp, công nghệ sinh học thế hệ mới ngày càng khẳng định vị trí động lực then chốt. Theo Quyết định số 1131/QĐ-TTg của Thủ tướng Chính phủ về Danh mục công nghệ chiến lược và sản phẩm công nghệ chiến lược, công nghệ chỉnh sửa gen thuộc nhóm công nghệ y - sinh học tiên tiến, được định hướng ưu tiên ứng dụng mạnh mẽ trong y tế và nông nghiệp. items.title: Sở Khoa học và Công nghệ Hà Tĩnh hướng dẫn xét công nhận sáng kiến và đánh giá hiệu quả đề tài khoa học
items.summary: Theo hướng dẫn, các giải pháp được xem xét công nhận là sáng kiến bao gồm: giải pháp kỹ thuật, giải pháp quản lý, giải pháp tác nghiệp và giải pháp ứng dụng tiến bộ kỹ thuật. items.title: Andrej Karpathy:
items.summary:
Andrej Karpathy:

“A 1B model can be much more effective than most current LLMs.

90% of current models waste a ton of capacity and money on remembering stuff that doesn’t matter.”

here is his 5 core thesis about Small LLM’s:

1. the intelligence was never the knowledge. Strip the memorized internet, keep the reasoning. What’s left is the cognitive core, and it’s small.

2. the core might fit in ~1B params. Maybe less. “Plenty of room at the bottom.” We’ve been paying for a library when we needed a brain.

3. size stopped being the bottleneck. What makes an agent work is the tools it can call and how tight the feedback loop is, not parameter count.

4. intelligence lives in the system, not the weights. A raw LLM is a CPU with no OS. Small core + good harness > giant model alone.

5. you can own it. A model on your hardware is one no one can rate-limit, price-hike, or deprecate on you.

in 12 months the gap between teams shipping on-device and teams paying per-token frontier bills won’t be capability.

TwIL an 8.8B model at 90%+ of frontier isn’t a benchmark flex.

It’s the thesis Karpathy’s been repeating all year, made real.

His postdoctoral students Eric Kaiyuan Chen and Shuangyu Xie gave Astra access to their simulation interface and a short video of a real robot whose assignment was using a sponge to wipe ink off a metal bar. items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.
